subject: Post-call: BrightCart perf acceptance criteria + reproducibility action register
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jeff Tan <jeff@brightcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — perf targets and reproducibility

Hi Jeff — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the SLO/benchmark plan: 

Key perf targets you confirmed on the call:
- P95 latency (token gen) target: <= 120ms for short interactive requests (~200 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: 120 QPS (batched) at 99% availability during peak retail windows
- Streaming requirement: server-sent partial tokens within 60ms of generation start for UI streaming
- Concurrency: 48 concurrent sessions with KV cache warm-up profile

What we need from BrightCart to run a reproducible benchmark:
1) Canonical prompt set (representative user flows) — you said you can share a seed subset this week.
2) A small sample corpus for context (checkout + recommendations examples).
3) Preferred test windows (timezone and blackout windows) — you mentioned US-Eastern weekday 0200–0500 UTC works.
4) Success definition: you preferred a rolling 1-hour window for throughput SLO validation.

Proposed Redwood deliverables next: 
- Benchmark harness manifest (measurement definitions + script knobs) — draft by Mon, 24 Aug.
- Run plan (warm-up, cache custody, quantization variants) and a reproducibility checklist.
- A short deck summarizing acceptance criteria we can share with your Ops.

Can you confirm the prompts and the test window? If possible attach one representative prompt file (5–10 prompts) so we can validate harness parsing.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Monica/Ben on the run plan once we have the seed prompts.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(redwood-bio and contact)

Attachment: brightcart-prompt-sample-v1.json (stub)

From: Jeff Tan <jeff@brightcart.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — perf targets and reproducibility

Thanks Rishi — good summary. Confirming the items below and attaching the initial prompt seed.

Confirmed targets:
- P95 <= 120ms (short interactive) — agreed.
- Sustained 120 QPS — yes, this reflects our checkout/rate-limiting peak.
- Streaming: early partials within 60ms — this is important for our mobile UX.
- Concurrency: 48 sessions, but if you can test 64 as a stretch that’d be useful.

Attached: brightcart-prompt-sample-v1.json (5 canonical prompts + metadata).
Test window: We prefer the first run during 02:00–05:00 UTC (US-Eastern off-peak).
Pass criteria: rolling 1-hour windows for throughput; latency SLO should hold for at least 95% of 1-hour windows during the run.

Notes on custody and data: these prompts are synthetic slices from anonymized logs; avoid storing full context after the run. SOC2-compliant handling is required — we can sign any temporary access constraints if needed.

-Jeff
Head of Platform, BrightCart

Attachment: brightcart-prompt-sample-v1.json (stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap & next steps — perf targets and reproducibility

Monica / Ben — forwarding Jeff’s confirmation and seed prompts. Action items I propose below.

Action register:
- Monica: draft the Benchmark Harness Manifest (measurement definitions + reproducibility checklist). Target: Mon 24 Aug EOD.
- Ben: prepare 2 run-configs: (A) baseline FP16 (no quant), (B) int8 quantized variant. Include continuous batching profiles. Target: Tue 25 Aug morning.
- Rishi (me): produce the short acceptance deck and coordinate the 02:00–05:00 UTC run window with BrightCart.

Important reproducibility notes to include in manifest (quick bullets):
- Random seeds and model version pinned (exact git hash or model artifact id).
- KV cache custody rules: how we reuse cache across sessions during warm-up vs. fresh start tests.
- Measurement epoch: 10-minute micro-windows inside the rolling 1-hour validation windows.
- All raw logs + perf traces stored to the drive link for audit (redacted per BrightCart request).

I attached our initial deck draft and a CSV load matrix (streaming-loadmatrix.csv) with consumer distributions. Please review and mark any missing knobs you need.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a short run coordination call with Jeff for Mon afternoon if that works.

Rishi

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-deck-v1.pdf, streaming-loadmatrix.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap & next steps — perf targets and reproducibility

Quick technical clarifications / asks before we lock configs: 

1) Streaming measurement: do we treat the streaming SLO as measured from request arrival -> first partial token emitted, or from first token generation -> client delivery? I assume request arrival -> first partial token (that includes network egress). Confirming because it changes how we instrument the harness.

2) KV cache warm-up profile: Jeff gave us an 80% warm cache expectation for steady state. For reproducibility we should run two modes: 'cold-start' (fresh model, zero cache) and 'steady' (simulate 80% warm cache with synthetic warmups). I’ll prepare both.

3) For quantized runs, do we allow fallbacks to non-quantized model if quality regressions exceed threshold? If yes, we need the exact quality metric and threshold (BLEU / embedding sim) BrightCart will accept.

I’ll hold off on running until we get Jeff’s confirmation on the streaming definition and the fallback policy.

-Ben
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jeff Tan <jeff@brightcart.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap & next steps — perf targets and reproducibility

Thanks Ben — answers below: 

1) Streaming measurement: measure from request arrival -> first partial token emitted (client egress included). That’s the number our mobile team will use to gate UX.

2) KV cache modes: yes, run both cold-start and steady (80% warm). For steady-state please reuse the same warmup script we discussed; I attached a short snippet in the Drive link.

3) Quantization fallback policy: allowed if quality delta (embedding cosine similarity on a 250-sample eval set) stays >= 0.985 relative to FP baseline. If below that, do not promote quantized variant for production traffic.

Test coordination: go ahead and schedule the first run on Tue 2026-08-25 02:30 UTC (should be within our 02:00–05:00 window). Let me know the exact run id and we’ll monitor.

Looking forward — thanks for moving fast on this.

Jeff
Head of Platform, BrightCart

Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1AqBenchmarkDeck (run scripts + warmup snippet)
